title: Proper self-product exchange commutes with the canonical forget-supports isomorphisms
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $f:X\to S$ a proper morphism of arbitrary schemes. Work in the ordinary unbounded small-etale derived categories of $A$-modules [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. Put $U=X\times_S X$, $p=\operatorname{pr}_1$, $v=\operatorname{pr}_2$, and write $F_h=Lh^*$, $R_h=Rh_*$, $R_h^!=Rh_!$ (the superscript here denotes compact supports, not the exceptional inverse image). Let $c_h:R_h^!\xrightarrow{\sim}R_h$ be the canonical proper forget-supports comparison [def-sp-unbounded-proper-shriek-star-comparison]. Let $\beta_f:F_fR_f^!\xrightarrow{\sim}R_p^!F_v$ be the compact-support exchange of the flipped self-pullback square [def-sf-supported-diagonal-calculus], and let $E_f:F_fR_f\to R_pF_v$ be its canonical ordinary exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ one has, in application order,
$$\beta_f(K);c_p(F_vK)=F_f(c_f(K));E_f(K).$$
Equivalently, since ordinary exchange is invertible for finite coefficients [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring],
$$\beta_f(K)^{-1};F_f(c_f(K))=c_p(F_vK);E_f(K)^{-1}.$$
Both equations concern the actual chosen-compactification maps; no boundedness, finite-type base, nonempty-base or trace hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Specialize proper_exchange to the flipped self-product square. The first projection is proper by proper base change. By definition SfDiagonalKernel.exchangeFirst is asIso of the compact-support exchange, and CoordinateTrace.exchange1 is asIso of the ordinary exchange, using the finite-coefficient proper-base-change instance. Their hom components are the exchange maps just used. The ordinaryFinitePullback functors are definitionally the same left-derived inverse images. This proves the forward equation without extra hypotheses.

proof.text: Precompose the desired inverse equation with the hom of SfDiagonalKernel.exchangeFirst at K. Cancel its hom-inverse pair, substitute the forward equation, and cancel the hom-inverse pair of CoordinateTrace.exchange1. This proves the second conjunct. These are isomorphism cancellation identities, valid also for empty schemes and zero coefficients.
